models.name: discussion_board_article_categories
models.description:
Article category master data for the economic and political discussion board.

This table stores normalized category definitions such as "Economy" or "Politics" that are used to classify articles for browsing, filtering, and reporting. Each category has a stable machine-friendly code and a human-readable name so that application logic and external integrations can rely on a consistent identifier while users see localized or readable labels.

Categories are managed by administrators rather than end users. Articles in {@link discussion_board_articles} will reference these categories through a foreign key, ensuring consistent classification across the system. Soft deletion via deleted_at allows categories to be retired without breaking historical article data, while created_at and updated_at support basic audit and ordering use cases.

primaryField.name: id
primaryField.description: Primary Key. Unique identifier for each article category, generated as a UUID to ensure global uniqueness across the system.

plainFields.name: code
plainFields.description:
Machine-friendly unique code for the category, such as "ECONOMY" or "POLITICS".

This value is used by backend logic, integrations, and configuration as a stable identifier that does not change even if the display name is edited.

plainFields.name: name
plainFields.description:
Human-readable name of the article category as displayed to users, such as "Economy" or "Politics".

This field is what users typically see in article creation forms and filter dropdowns.

plainFields.name: description
plainFields.description:
Optional longer description of what the category is intended for.

This text helps administrators and possibly users understand the scope or examples of content that belong in the category.

plainFields.name: order
plainFields.description:
Integer value used to define the display order of categories in lists and dropdowns.

Lower numbers typically appear first. This allows administrators to control the default ordering without relying solely on creation time or name.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description:
Timestamp indicating when the category was created.

Used for audit purposes and to support chronological listings where needed.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description:
Timestamp indicating when the category was last updated.

Updated whenever the category’s editable fields (such as name or description) change.

plainFields.name: deleted_at
plainFields.description:
Nullable timestamp indicating when the category was soft-deleted or retired.

When this field is non-null, the category should no longer be offered for new article assignment, but existing articles may continue to reference it for historical integrity.

uniqueIndexes.description: Ensures that each article category code is unique across the system so that business logic and integrations can rely on a single stable identifier per category.

plainIndexes.description: Composite index used for efficiently listing categories in display order while also supporting queries that paginate or filter by creation time.

ginIndexes.description: GIN/trigram index on the category name to support simple text search and fuzzy matching when filtering or searching categories by name in administrative tools.

models.name: discussion_board_guestusers
models.description:
Guest user placeholder accounts for unauthenticated visitors.

Represents optional persisted identities for guests when the system chooses to maintain long-lived guest records, for example for future migration to full member accounts or to correlate anonymous activity under privacy rules.

In the current business requirements, guests do not authenticate or hold permissions beyond read-only access, so this table remains minimal and is rarely manipulated directly by user-facing APIs.

primaryField.name: id
primaryField.description: Primary key. Uniquely identifies a guest user placeholder record.

plainFields.name: anonymous_token
plainFields.description: Opaque token or fingerprint that represents this guest user across visits. Used only if the system chooses to persist guest identity for correlation or migration.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this guest user record was created.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this guest user record was last updated.

plainFields.name: deleted_at
plainFields.description: Soft deletion timestamp. When set, this guest user record is considered closed or no longer in active use.

models.name: discussion_board_memberusers
models.description:
Registered member accounts for the discussionBoard service.

Stores authentication credentials, basic profile fields, and high-level lifecycle state for member users who create and manage their own articles, comments, and attachments.

This table underpins permissions and moderation behavior, including account status flags that interact with restriction policies and suspension rules defined in the business requirements.

primaryField.name: id
primaryField.description: Primary key. Uniquely identifies a member user account.

plainFields.name: email
plainFields.description: Member email address used as the primary contact field and login identifier. Must be unique among member users.

plainFields.name: password_hash
plainFields.description: Hashed credential used for authenticating the member user. Plain-text passwords are never stored.

plainFields.name: display_name
plainFields.description: Public display name or nickname shown alongside articles and comments created by this member user.

plainFields.name: bio
plainFields.description: Optional short self-introduction text that the member can provide on their profile.

plainFields.name: location
plainFields.description: Optional free-text field representing geographic location or main interest area, treated as plain descriptive text.

plainFields.name: email_verified
plainFields.description: Indicates whether the member user has completed email verification.

plainFields.name: account_status
plainFields.description: High-level lifecycle state of the account, such as active, suspended, closed, or banned. Used together with restriction records to enforce behavior.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this member user account was created.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this member user account record was last updated.

plainFields.name: deleted_at
plainFields.description: Soft deletion timestamp. When set, the account is considered closed from a business perspective while historical content may remain.

plainFields.name: last_login_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp of the last successful login for this member user, used for account lifecycle and security monitoring.

plainFields.name: closed_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the account was explicitly closed, either by the member user or by an administrator.

plainFields.name: closed_by_admin
plainFields.description: Flag indicating whether the closure was initiated by an administrator instead of the account owner.

models.name: discussion_board_adminusers
models.description:
Administrator accounts for managing content and users in discussionBoard.

Stores authentication credentials, basic profile fields, and lifecycle state for administrative users who can moderate content, process reports, and manage member accounts.

Admin accounts have broader permissions but are still subject to standard authentication and audit requirements.

primaryField.name: id
primaryField.description: Primary key. Uniquely identifies an administrator account.

plainFields.name: email
plainFields.description: Administrator email address used for authentication and critical notifications. Must be unique among administrators.

plainFields.name: password_hash
plainFields.description: Hashed credential used to authenticate the administrator. Plain-text passwords are never stored.

plainFields.name: display_name
plainFields.description: Public or semi-public display name used when this administrator creates content or appears in audit trails.

plainFields.name: bio
plainFields.description: Optional short profile or role description for this administrator account.

plainFields.name: email_verified
plainFields.description: Indicates whether the administrator has completed email verification.

plainFields.name: account_status
plainFields.description: Lifecycle state for the administrator account, such as active, suspended, or closed, used for access control.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this administrator account was created.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this administrator account record was last updated.

plainFields.name: deleted_at
plainFields.description: Soft deletion timestamp. When set, the administrator account is no longer usable, while audit references remain valid.

plainFields.name: last_login_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp of the last successful login for this administrator account.

models.name: discussion_board_memberuser_sessions
models.description:
Session records for authenticated memberUser accounts.

Captures minimal connection context for each member session, including IP, entry URL, and referrer, to support audit trails and basic security analysis.

This table follows the global session table pattern and is treated as a subsidiary entity used only for tracing and not for direct business workflows.

primaryField.name: id
primaryField.description: Primary key. Uniquely identifies a member user session.

foreignFields.name: discussion_board_memberuser_id
foreignFields.description: Reference to the member user who owns this session. {@link discussion_board_memberusers.id}.

plainFields.name: ip
plainFields.description: IP address from which the member user established this session.

plainFields.name: href
plainFields.description: Full URL that the user accessed when this session was created.

plainFields.name: referrer
plainFields.description: Referrer URL, if any, that led the user into the application for this session.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this session was created.

plainFields.name: expired_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this session was considered expired or terminated. Null while still active.

models.name: discussion_board_adminuser_sessions
models.description:
Session records for authenticated adminUser accounts.

Stores minimal session context for administrators, capturing connection data needed for auditing privileged operations and monitoring admin activity.

Follows the global session table pattern and acts as a subsidiary entity referenced from admin logic but not directly manipulated by end users.

primaryField.name: id
primaryField.description: Primary key. Uniquely identifies an admin user session.

foreignFields.name: discussion_board_adminuser_id
foreignFields.description: Reference to the administrator who owns this session. {@link discussion_board_adminusers.id}.

plainFields.name: ip
plainFields.description: IP address from which the admin user established this session.

plainFields.name: href
plainFields.description: Full URL that the administrator accessed when this session was created.

plainFields.name: referrer
plainFields.description: Referrer URL, if any, that led the administrator into the application for this session.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this admin session was created.

plainFields.name: expired_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this admin session was considered expired or terminated. Null while still active.

models.name: discussion_board_memberuser_restrictions
models.description:
Current restriction state for each memberUser account.

Represents simple moderation-driven account restrictions such as posting restriction or full block, which determine whether a member user may create articles, comments, or attachments.

This table holds at most one active restriction record per member user and includes metadata for reason categorization and timing; it is managed by administrative workflows when applying or lifting restrictions.

primaryField.name: id
primaryField.description: Primary key. Uniquely identifies a restriction record for a member user.

foreignFields.name: discussion_board_memberuser_id
foreignFields.description: Reference to the member user subject to this restriction. One restriction record per member user. {@link discussion_board_memberusers.id}.

plainFields.name: restriction_level
plainFields.description: Level of restriction applied to the member user, such as posting_restriction or full_block.

plainFields.name: reason_category
plainFields.description: High-level category describing why the restriction was applied, for example repeated_violations, hate_abuse, or spam_advertising.

plainFields.name: started_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this restriction became effective for the member user.

plainFields.name: ended_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this restriction was lifted. Null while the restriction remains active.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this restriction record was created.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this restriction record was last updated.

models.name: discussion_board_articles
models.description:
Core articles representing economic and political discussion topics.

This table stores the primary discussion objects that users browse, search, read, create, edit, and delete. Each record represents one article with its title, body, optional summary, category assignment, moderation state, and audit timestamps.

Authorship is modeled through subtype tables {@link discussion_board_article_of_memberusers} and {@link discussion_board_article_of_adminusers}, allowing either a member user or an admin user to own the article without using nullable polymorphic foreign keys.

Articles are subject to moderation and can move between business states such as Active, Hidden, and Deleted. Soft deletion is implemented using the deleted_at field, while moderation_state records the current visibility state from a business perspective.

Articles are linked to categories via {@link discussion_board_article_categories} to support simple filtering and navigation. Per-member like engagement is represented in {@link discussion_board_article_likes}. Any aggregated metrics or counters for views or likes should be implemented in separate materialized views, not in this primary table.

primaryField.name: id
primaryField.description: Primary key of the article. Unique identifier for each discussion article.

foreignFields.name: discussion_board_article_category_id
foreignFields.description: Foreign key referencing the category of this article. {@link discussion_board_article_categories.id}. Each article belongs to exactly one primary category.

plainFields.name: title
plainFields.description: Human-readable title of the article. Must be non-empty and respect minimum and maximum length constraints for article titles.

plainFields.name: body
plainFields.description: Main body text of the article. Contains the full discussion content written by the author and must satisfy length constraints defined for article bodies.

plainFields.name: summary
plainFields.description: Optional short plain-text summary of the article. Used in listings or previews and limited to a small maximum length. Nullable when no summary is provided.

plainFields.name: moderation_state
plainFields.description: Business moderation state of the article. Expected values conceptually include "Active", "Hidden", and "Deleted" to represent visibility and moderation decisions. Enforcement of allowed values is handled in application logic.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the article was first created. Used for sorting lists and audit purposes.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp of the most recent successful update to the article content or metadata. Equal to created_at for never-edited articles.

plainFields.name: deleted_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the article was logically deleted from a data-retention perspective. Nullable; when set, the article should be treated as Deleted in business workflows and excluded from normal listings.

models.name: discussion_board_article_of_memberusers
models.description:
Authorship subtype linking articles to member users.

This table represents the ownership of articles created by regular member users. Each record connects exactly one article in {@link discussion_board_articles} with exactly one member user in {@link discussion_board_memberusers}.

The 1:1 relationship between an article and this subtype is enforced with a unique constraint on discussion_board_article_id, ensuring that a given article has at most one memberUser author record. Articles authored by admins use the separate {@link discussion_board_article_of_adminusers} table.

This design follows the main-entity plus subtype pattern to avoid nullable polymorphic foreign keys and to keep ownership constraints explicit at the database level.

primaryField.name: id
primaryField.description: Primary key of the member user authorship record.

foreignFields.name: discussion_board_article_id
foreignFields.description: Foreign key referencing the article authored by a member user. {@link discussion_board_articles.id}. Unique to enforce a 1:1 relationship between an article and this subtype row.

foreignFields.name: discussion_board_memberuser_id
foreignFields.description: Foreign key referencing the member user who authored the article. {@link discussion_board_memberusers.id}. Many articles can be authored by the same member user.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this authorship link was created. Typically identical to the article creation time for member-authored articles.

models.name: discussion_board_article_of_adminusers
models.description:
Authorship subtype linking articles to admin users.

This table represents the ownership of articles created by administrators. Each record connects exactly one article in {@link discussion_board_articles} with exactly one admin user in {@link discussion_board_adminusers}.

The 1:1 relationship between an article and this subtype is enforced with a unique constraint on discussion_board_article_id, ensuring that a given article has at most one adminUser author record. Articles authored by regular members use the separate {@link discussion_board_article_of_memberusers} table.

Using this subtype avoids nullable polymorphic foreign keys, keeping authorship constraints and relations explicit and fully normalized.

primaryField.name: id
primaryField.description: Primary key of the admin user authorship record.

foreignFields.name: discussion_board_article_id
foreignFields.description: Foreign key referencing the article authored by an admin user. {@link discussion_board_articles.id}. Unique to enforce a 1:1 relationship between an article and this subtype row.

foreignFields.name: discussion_board_adminuser_id
foreignFields.description: Foreign key referencing the admin user who authored the article. {@link discussion_board_adminusers.id}. Many articles can be authored by the same admin user.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this authorship link was created. Typically identical to the article creation time for admin-authored articles.

models.name: discussion_board_article_likes
models.description:
Per-member like engagement records for articles.

This table stores individual like actions performed by member users on articles. Each record represents that a specific member user has liked a specific article, with a creation timestamp for audit and ordering.

A unique composite constraint on (discussion_board_article_id, discussion_board_memberuser_id) ensures that a member user can like a given article at most once. Removing a like can be modeled by deleting the corresponding row.

This structure supports queries such as whether a member has liked a particular article, listing all likes made by a member, and aggregating like counts per article. Only member users can like articles; admin users can moderate content but do not require separate like ownership modeling.

primaryField.name: id
primaryField.description: Primary key of the article like record.

foreignFields.name: discussion_board_article_id
foreignFields.description: Foreign key referencing the liked article. {@link discussion_board_articles.id}. Many likes can reference the same article.

foreignFields.name: discussion_board_memberuser_id
foreignFields.description: Foreign key referencing the member user who liked the article. {@link discussion_board_memberusers.id}. Many likes can be created by the same member user.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the like was created. Used for audit trails and ordering of engagement activity.

models.name: discussion_board_comments
models.description:
Top-level text comments attached directly to discussion board articles.

This model stores the core business data for each comment, including its article relationship, text body, author type discriminator, moderation status, and lifecycle timestamps.

Each comment belongs to exactly one article and is authored either by a member user or an admin user via the polymorphic ownership pattern. The concrete author relationship details are held in the subsidiary tables {@link discussion_board_comment_of_memberusers} and {@link discussion_board_comment_of_adminusers}.

Moderation uses a simple status field (for example, Active, Hidden, Deleted) together with soft deletion to control visibility in lists and article views while preserving auditability for administrators.

primaryField.name: id
primaryField.description: Primary key of the comment. Uniquely identifies a discussion comment record.

foreignFields.name: discussion_board_article_id
foreignFields.description: Foreign key to the article this comment belongs to. {@link discussion_board_articles.id}. The comment is always attached to a single, existing article.

plainFields.name: author_type
plainFields.description: Logical type of the comment author. Expected values include "member" for member users and "admin" for admin users. Used for quick filtering and must be consistent with the corresponding ownership subtype table entry.

plainFields.name: body
plainFields.description: Text content of the comment. Must be non-empty and within business-defined length limits (for example, up to 5,000 visible characters).

plainFields.name: status
plainFields.description: Business-level moderation status of the comment. Typical values: "Active", "Hidden", or "Deleted". Controls visibility to regular users while allowing administrators to review handled content.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the comment was created. Used for ordering and audit trails.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the comment was last updated. Updated whenever the body or moderation-related fields change.

plainFields.name: deleted_at
plainFields.description: Soft deletion timestamp. When set, indicates that the comment is logically deleted and should be excluded from normal user views while still remaining in storage for audit or recovery purposes.

models.name: discussion_board_comment_of_memberusers
models.description:
Ownership subtype entity that links a comment to its member user author and the creating session.

This model implements the polymorphic ownership pattern for comments authored by regular member users. Each row represents a 1:1 extension of {@link discussion_board_comments} for comments whose actor type is a member user.

It records the member account that authored the comment, the session context at creation time, and a timestamp, allowing precise audit of which member and which session produced the comment without nullable foreign keys on the main comment table.

primaryField.name: id
primaryField.description: Primary key of the member user comment ownership record.

foreignFields.name: discussion_board_comment_id
foreignFields.description: Foreign key to the base comment entity. {@link discussion_board_comments.id}. Enforced as unique to ensure a strict 1:1 relationship for member-authored comments.

foreignFields.name: discussion_board_memberuser_id
foreignFields.description: Foreign key to the member user account that authored the comment. {@link discussion_board_memberusers.id}. Always required for member-authored comments.

foreignFields.name: discussion_board_memberuser_session_id
foreignFields.description: Foreign key to the member user session associated with the comment creation. {@link discussion_board_memberuser_sessions.id}. Captures connection context such as IP and referrer at creation time.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this ownership record was created. Typically matches the creation time of the underlying comment and is used for audit and traceability.

models.name: discussion_board_comment_of_adminusers
models.description:
Ownership subtype entity that links a comment to its admin user author and the creating session.

This model implements the polymorphic ownership pattern for comments authored by admin users. Each row represents a 1:1 extension of {@link discussion_board_comments} for comments whose actor type is an administrator.

It records the admin account that authored the comment, the session context at creation time, and a timestamp so that administrative commentary can be audited separately from member commentary without nullable foreign keys on the main comment table.

primaryField.name: id
primaryField.description: Primary key of the admin user comment ownership record.

foreignFields.name: discussion_board_comment_id
foreignFields.description: Foreign key to the base comment entity. {@link discussion_board_comments.id}. Enforced as unique to ensure a strict 1:1 relationship for admin-authored comments.

foreignFields.name: discussion_board_adminuser_id
foreignFields.description: Foreign key to the admin user account that authored the comment. {@link discussion_board_adminusers.id}. Always required for admin-authored comments.

foreignFields.name: discussion_board_adminuser_session_id
foreignFields.description: Foreign key to the admin user session associated with the comment creation. {@link discussion_board_adminuser_sessions.id}. Captures connection context such as IP and referrer at creation time.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this ownership record was created. Typically matches the creation time of the underlying comment and is used for audit and traceability of administrative actions.

models.name: discussion_board_attachments
models.description:
File attachments associated with discussion board articles.

This table stores metadata for images and documents that are attached to individual articles in the economic/political discussion board. Each row represents a single file that belongs to exactly one article, and the attachment has no lifecycle independent of its parent article.

The model records user-visible filename, MIME-like content type, file size, a display order within the parent article, and a URI pointing to the stored object. It also tracks a simple moderation status that aligns with article/content states such as Active, Hidden, and Deleted, as well as standard temporal audit fields.

Attachments are always managed through article operations or administration tools and are not directly searchable as a standalone resource for end users. They follow the visibility of their parent article while allowing administrators to hide or delete individual files when necessary.

primaryField.name: id
primaryField.description: Primary key. Unique identifier for the attachment record.

foreignFields.name: discussion_board_article_id
foreignFields.description: Parent article that this attachment belongs to. {@link discussion_board_articles.id}.

plainFields.name: file_uri
plainFields.description: URI location of the stored file object. Used by the application to retrieve or stream the attachment content.

plainFields.name: file_name
plainFields.description: Original or user-visible file name of the attachment. May be normalized for safety while remaining recognizable to users.

plainFields.name: content_type
plainFields.description: MIME-like content type of the attachment, such as "image/jpeg" or "application/pdf". Used to decide preview vs download behavior.

plainFields.name: file_size
plainFields.description: Size of the attachment file in bytes. Used for enforcing per-file and per-article size limits and for displaying approximate size to users.

plainFields.name: order_in_article
plainFields.description: Display order index of this attachment within its parent article. Lower values are shown earlier in attachment lists.

plainFields.name: status
plainFields.description: Moderation and lifecycle status of the attachment. Typical values mirror content states such as "active", "hidden", or "deleted" as defined by business rules.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the attachment record was created. Represents the time the file was first associated with the article.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the attachment record was last updated. Updated whenever metadata or status changes.

plainFields.name: deleted_at
plainFields.description: Soft deletion timestamp. When set, indicates the attachment is considered deleted for business purposes even if metadata is retained internally.

models.name: discussion_board_reports
models.description:
Central entity representing a single user report about an article, comment, or attachment.

Each row captures the reporting user type, target content type, reason category, optional free-text explanation, and the current moderation status and action chosen by administrators.

Moderation workflows use this table as the primary queue for reviewing reported content, changing statuses from submitted through in_review to resolved, and applying actions such as keeping, hiding, deleting content, or restricting the owning member user.

Reports are append-only audit records; they are not soft-deleted, and their lifecycle is independent from the lifecycle of the underlying content or reporting account.

primaryField.name: id
primaryField.description: Primary key of the report. Uniquely identifies a single report instance.

plainFields.name: target_type
plainFields.description: Discriminator describing which type of content this report targets. Typical values are "article", "comment", or "attachment" and are enforced at the application layer.

plainFields.name: reporter_type
plainFields.description: Discriminator describing which actor type submitted the report. Typical values are "memberuser" or "adminuser" and are enforced at the application layer.

plainFields.name: reason_code
plainFields.description: Machine-friendly code representing the primary reason category for this report. Example values include "hate_abuse", "harassment", "spam", "off_topic", "dangerous_misleading", and "other". Validation for allowed values is handled in the application.

plainFields.name: description
plainFields.description: Optional free-text explanation provided by the reporter to clarify the reason. Required by business rules when reason_code is "other", but stored as nullable at schema level.

plainFields.name: status
plainFields.description: Current workflow status of the report. Typical values are "submitted", "in_review", or "resolved". Used to drive admin report queues and filtering.

plainFields.name: action
plainFields.description: Administrative decision applied in response to this report. Example values include "none", "keep", "hide_content", "delete_content", and "restrict_user". Business rules determine valid combinations with status.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the report was created and submitted by the reporting user.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the report was last updated, typically when an admin changes status or action.

models.name: discussion_board_report_of_articles
models.description:
Link entity that associates a report with a specific article.

Each row connects exactly one {@link discussion_board_reports} record to exactly one {@link discussion_board_articles} record, enforcing a 1:1 relationship between the report and its article target while allowing many reports per article overall.

This table exists purely to normalize the polymorphic target relationship for article-type reports and is always managed through the main report or article workflows.

primaryField.name: id
primaryField.description: Primary key of the article-report link. Uniquely identifies the association between a report and an article.

foreignFields.name: discussion_board_report_id
foreignFields.description: Foreign key referencing the report that targets an article. Enforces that each report links to at most one article association. {@link discussion_board_reports.id}.

foreignFields.name: discussion_board_article_id
foreignFields.description: Foreign key referencing the article that was reported. Multiple reports can reference the same article through separate link rows. {@link discussion_board_articles.id}.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this report-to-article association was created. Typically matches the report creation time but is stored separately for consistency.

models.name: discussion_board_report_of_comments
models.description:
Link entity that associates a report with a specific comment.

Each row connects exactly one {@link discussion_board_reports} record to exactly one {@link discussion_board_comments} record, enforcing a 1:1 relationship between the report and its comment target while permitting many reports for the same comment.

This table normalizes the polymorphic target relationship for comment-type reports and is always manipulated via the main report or comment management flows.

primaryField.name: id
primaryField.description: Primary key of the comment-report link. Uniquely identifies the association between a report and a comment.

foreignFields.name: discussion_board_report_id
foreignFields.description: Foreign key referencing the report that targets a comment. Enforces that each report links to at most one comment association. {@link discussion_board_reports.id}.

foreignFields.name: discussion_board_comment_id
foreignFields.description: Foreign key referencing the comment that was reported. Multiple reports can reference the same comment through separate link rows. {@link discussion_board_comments.id}.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this report-to-comment association was created.

models.name: discussion_board_report_of_attachments
models.description:
Link entity that associates a report with a specific attachment belonging to an article.

Each row connects exactly one {@link discussion_board_reports} record to exactly one {@link discussion_board_attachments} record, maintaining a 1:1 relationship between the report and its attachment target while allowing multiple reports per attachment.

This table isolates attachment-specific relationships so that the main report entity does not require nullable foreign keys for different target types.

primaryField.name: id
primaryField.description: Primary key of the attachment-report link. Uniquely identifies the association between a report and an attachment.

foreignFields.name: discussion_board_report_id
foreignFields.description: Foreign key referencing the report that targets an attachment. Ensures at most one attachment association per report. {@link discussion_board_reports.id}.

foreignFields.name: discussion_board_attachment_id
foreignFields.description: Foreign key referencing the attachment that was reported. Many reports can reference the same attachment via different link rows. {@link discussion_board_attachments.id}.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this report-to-attachment association was created.

models.name: discussion_board_report_of_memberusers
models.description:
Link entity that associates a report with a member user as the reporting actor.

Each row connects exactly one {@link discussion_board_reports} record to exactly one {@link discussion_board_memberusers} record, forming a 1:1 relationship between the report and its memberUser reporter while still allowing a single member user to submit many reports.

This table normalizes the polymorphic reporter relationship for member users and ensures there are no nullable reporter foreign keys on the main report entity.

primaryField.name: id
primaryField.description: Primary key of the member-user reporter link. Uniquely identifies the association between a report and its memberUser reporter.

foreignFields.name: discussion_board_report_id
foreignFields.description: Foreign key referencing the report submitted by a member user. Ensures at most one memberUser association per report. {@link discussion_board_reports.id}.

foreignFields.name: discussion_board_memberuser_id
foreignFields.description: Foreign key referencing the member user account that filed the report. A single member user can be associated with many reports. {@link discussion_board_memberusers.id}.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this report-to-memberUser association was created.

models.name: discussion_board_report_of_adminusers
models.description:
Link entity that associates a report with an admin user as the reporting actor.

While most reports are expected from member users, administrators may also file reports when acting as regular users. Each row connects one {@link discussion_board_reports} record to one {@link discussion_board_adminusers} record, enforcing a 1:1 relationship between the report and its adminUser reporter.

This table complements {@link discussion_board_report_of_memberusers} to fully normalize the polymorphic reporter relationship across actor types.

primaryField.name: id
primaryField.description: Primary key of the admin-user reporter link. Uniquely identifies the association between a report and its adminUser reporter.

foreignFields.name: discussion_board_report_id
foreignFields.description: Foreign key referencing the report submitted by an admin user. Ensures at most one adminUser association per report. {@link discussion_board_reports.id}.

foreignFields.name: discussion_board_adminuser_id
foreignFields.description: Foreign key referencing the admin user account that filed the report. A single admin user can be associated with many reports. {@link discussion_board_adminusers.id}.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this report-to-adminUser association was created.

models.name: discussion_board_memberuser_notification_preferences
models.description:
Notification preference settings for a single member user account.

Stores per-member configuration flags controlling which categories of notifications the system is allowed to send, such as activity on the user’s own content, digest summaries, and optional marketing or non-essential announcements.

Each record is strictly associated with exactly one {@link discussion_board_memberusers} row, forming a 1:1 relationship so that every member user can have at most one preference set.

Business logic uses these flags at send time to decide whether to deliver a notification, while mandatory service announcements remain governed by global policy rather than stored preferences.

primaryField.name: id
primaryField.description: Primary key of the member user notification preferences record.

foreignFields.name: discussion_board_memberuser_id
foreignFields.description: Owner member user account whose notification preferences are stored in this row. {@link discussion_board_memberusers.id}.

plainFields.name: activity_notifications_enabled
plainFields.description: Indicates whether the member user wishes to receive notifications about activity on their own content, such as replies to their articles or comments.

plainFields.name: digest_notifications_enabled
plainFields.description: Indicates whether the member user wishes to receive periodic digest or summary notifications that aggregate recent relevant activity.

plainFields.name: marketing_notifications_enabled
plainFields.description: Indicates whether the member user allows optional marketing-style or non-essential announcement notifications, separate from mandatory service announcements.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp recording when this notification preference record was first created.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp recording when this notification preference record was last updated.

models.name: discussion_board_adminuser_notification_preferences
models.description:
Notification preference settings for a single admin user account.

Stores per-admin configuration flags controlling which categories of notifications the system is allowed to send, such as notifications about activity on the admin’s own content, digest summaries, and optional marketing or non-essential announcements.

Each record is strictly associated with exactly one {@link discussion_board_adminusers} row, forming a 1:1 relationship so that every admin user can have at most one preference set.

While administrators must still receive mandatory service and policy communications, these flags allow fine-tuning of non-essential categories and reduce noise for operational accounts.

primaryField.name: id
primaryField.description: Primary key of the admin user notification preferences record.

foreignFields.name: discussion_board_adminuser_id
foreignFields.description: Owner admin user account whose notification preferences are stored in this row. {@link discussion_board_adminusers.id}.

plainFields.name: activity_notifications_enabled
plainFields.description: Indicates whether the admin user wishes to receive notifications about activity on content they authored, such as replies to their articles or comments.

plainFields.name: digest_notifications_enabled
plainFields.description: Indicates whether the admin user wishes to receive periodic digest or summary notifications that aggregate recent relevant activity or moderation-relevant events.

plainFields.name: marketing_notifications_enabled
plainFields.description: Indicates whether the admin user allows optional marketing-style or non-essential announcement notifications, separate from mandatory service or operator-critical messages.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp recording when this notification preference record was first created.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp recording when this notification preference record was last updated.
